details: The Dutchman, Captain William Jansz recorded his visit, in the Duyfken, to about 200 miles off the coastline from the Pennefather River to Cape Keerweer on Western Cape York Peninsula in Queensland. Upon landing at Batavia river to make observations, ‘the crew was attacked and one mortality, speared’.

This act of resistance to European visitors, the earliest in written record, was by a number of Tjungundji people whose country is located several kilometres south of the former location of Mapoon and who were familiar with outside visitors.

The Tjungundji share songs with a number of groups in Cape York, which demonstrate ceremonial links to the peoples of Papua New Guinea. For thousands of years intermarriage, cultural and technological exchange was conducted along trade routes which threaded north from the mainland and through the Torres Strait Islands.

title: Direct ICW envoy makes initial inquiry after Crimson Dunes local founding
summary: Draft event: in 1811, soon after Crimson Dunes is locally founded, a direct envoy or formal correspondence from the International Confederation of Wizards contacts the emerging Australian magical community about recognition, records, secrecy, school legitimacy, and governance.
sourceOriginalPath: Author alignment: ICW contact should happen soon after 1810; school-specific Book/Quill-style artefacts and wider ICW/Ministry registers may exist.
details: This should not mean immediate registration. It is the opening of formal contact or awareness.
Possible triggers: unusual student-detection records, reports from British magical arrivals, secrecy concerns, or school/founding correspondence.

Draft registry model: school-specific Book of Admittance / Quill of Acceptance style artefacts may feed or mirror a wider ICW/Ministry magical-child register. This supports later ICW/Ministry knowledge of magical users, broad locations, school eligibility, and possible wand/Trace linkage. Mechanism is draft worldbuilding, not canon.

Draft wand/Trace model: ICW-approved or Ministry-registered wands sold through approved wandmakers such as Ollivanders may carry or initialise a trace-like registry link. This is proposed Crimson Dunes adaptation and requires later rules review.
Author decision applied: first contact arrives through direct ICW envoy/correspondence, not through the British Ministry as intermediary.
australianImpactNotes: Directly affects the emerging Australian magical community by creating early international attention, possible reporting obligations, and institutional pressure around records and recognised schooling.
